data.title: Hedera price extends 7-week slide as HBAR bears maintain control below $0.0645
data.description:
Hedera [HBAR] has shed 3.79% in the past 24 hours, continuing its downtrend. In mid-October, the former support at $0.088 had been breached, setting off a steady wave of selling.

The past week’s market-wide volatility did not help HBAR bulls. At the time of writing, they were defending the $0.055 support zone.

In other news, it was reported that Canary Capital’s HBAR spot ETF, the only U.S. spot ETF offering exposure to Hedera’s native token, now holds around 549 million HBAR.

That was around 1.3% of the 43 billion circulating supply. It is long-term bullish for tokens to be accumulated in regulated infrastructure. But is it enough to halt the dominant downtrend?

Nearly 2 months of red sees HBAR fall to new lows

Hedera’s weekly price chart showed that the bulls tried to push prices past the $0.107 swing level from February. They tried twice and failed twice, with the latest attempt coming in September.

Since this rejection, the price has closed a weekly session below the $0.0645 swing low. Moreover, the price action showed a bearish long-term trend continuation.

Besides, the $0.0575 level, which had been an important support from November 2024, has also been breached.

Long-term HBAR investors might have to rethink their bullish bias following the steady losses and the altcoin’s inability to defend key demand zones.

Should HBAR traders sell the bounce?

The 4-hour chart showed that the $0.059 and $0.054 were the key horizontal levels to watch. The RSI was still below neutral 50, showing bears continue to have the upper hand.

The Stochastic RSI was about to form a bullish crossover, which could be followed by a price bounce. Swing traders can look to sell this bounce, if one appears and gets close to $0.058-$0.059.

A breakdown below $0.0548 will confirm further bearishness. Meanwhile, a breakout past $0.0594 will signal some respite to the downtrend and possibly a bigger bounce.

Final Summary

  • Canary Capital held a sizeable amount of HBAR, compared to the circulating supply in its spot ETF, which was a bullish sign.
  • Nevertheless, market-wide pessimism has resulted in 7 consecutive weekly bearish candles for the altcoin, confirming the long-term downtrend’s continuation.

data.title: Render outpaces Bitcoin and Ethereum – But its rebound can gather steam ONLY IF…
data.description:
Render [RENDER] was among the top gainers for the day in the crypto market. The native token of the decentralized GPU-based rendering solution provider network has rallied 4% for the day, comfortably surpassing the gains of the leaders, Bitcoin [BTC] and Ethereum [ETH], at 0.06% and 0.49%, respectively, at the time of writing.

Alongside its price move, the Open Interest was up by 9.15% for the day. A high OI uptick alongside a price bounce generally points to speculative buying and short-term bullish belief.

The spot CVD was also slowly climbing higher, while the funding rates remained close to zero, according to Coinalyze data. This meant that spot buying was beginning to recover, and the threat of a long squeeze on the back of the swift OI uptick was minimal.

In other news, Render participated in Solana’s Breakpoint 2026, showcasing its immersive digital art exhibition.

RENDER long-term consolidation not yet shaken off

Since December 2025, RENDER bulls have stubbornly defended the $1.24 support zone. Marked as the lows of a long-term range, the weekly chart above highlighted the lack of a decisive trend.

The OBV has been moving sideways since May and has not managed to set notable new highs or lows. The Awesome Oscillator also meandered about the zero line, unlike October-November of 2025 when bearish momentum was dominant.

The $1.24 support, range high of $2.60, and the mid-range level at $1.92 (close to the $2.0 supply zone) were worth investor scrutiny for price trend clues.

Retest of former local floor colors short-term RENDER outlook

The 4-hour chart was more encouraging for traders as there was a noticeable price trend. The OBV had slipped considerably earlier this month, a result of the market-wide sell-off towards the end of the previous week.

The $1.45-$1.50 former support zone has now been retested as a supply zone. It is likely that RENDER would continue its H4 downtrend and seek the $1.31 lows next.

Final Summary

  • The Render short-term speculative belief appeared to be bullish following Tuesday’s 11.56% price rally.
  • The 4-hour chart highlighted why bears were likely in control of the market, while the weekly chart illuminated a long-term range formation.

data.title: What is Ethereum actually for? A judge and Vitalik Buterin both left it open
data.description:
the 16th of November, a federal judge acquitted Anton and James Peraire-Bueno in the “first of its kind” wire fraud prosecution over a $25 million Ethereum exploit. This judgement came about after the government failed to prove the brothers made any “material misrepresentation.”

The ruling, filed in the Southern District of New York (24-CR-293), came the same day as when Bitwise CEO Hunter Horsley pitched stablecoins as a backup for banks.

On a similar note, Ethereum [ETH] co-founder Vitalik Buterin argued that digital assets do not match up to investing in houses. These three developments, when taken together, compound the question of what crypto is actually for.

What was the case about?

On the 2nd of April 2023, the brothers seemingly exploited a bug in the MEV-Boost relay software, due to which they could view transactions that sandwich traders believed were private.

The brothers’ alleged proposal for replacement transactions, in turn, resulted in massive losses of roughly $25 million within seconds.

The government called the prosecution,

The very first of its kind.

Finally, on the 16th of November 2026, Judge Jessica G. L. Clarke, when granting an acquittal, wrote,

The question before the Court is not whether the Peraire-Buenos’ conduct was right or moral, or even whether it violated uncharged crimes.

She continued,

It is simply whether the evidence at trial, construed in a light most favorable to the Government, could support wire fraud and related convictions in this case. Because the Government failed to prove that the Peraire-Buenos made any material misrepresentations in the execution of their scheme, the motion is granted.

The court analyzed the government’s theories – including the “lure transactions” and the so-called “false signature,” and found nothing that could support a wire fraud conviction.

What are crypto’s varying use cases?

A couple of days later, on the 18th of November, Horsley posted on X:

Rolling bank outages in the AI era – Consider having some stablecoins or crypto just in case.

The post came as thousands of Chase, Bank of America, and Wells Fargo customers reported being unable to access their accounts.

Vitalik Buterin, in a separate post on November 18, argued that younger generations have been investing in digital assets over real estate options; doing so, he noted, reduces –

Perverse incentives that drive people to push to keep housing expensive.

But he added a condition: housing had the advantage of being –

A culture and policy-encouraged default of investing in a safe non-crazy thing that you can’t easily liquidate.

He also wrote,

Modern platforms encourage the opposite of this, leading to more irresponsible behavior… We need the equivalent of those good properties that housing investment has, for modern digital assets.

Is crypto unequivalent to TradFi?

The three developments have been framing crypto’s developing role separately, but these assets have a long way to go before they can fully replace TradFi.

Vitalik Buterin himself leaves the question open, as he observed,

We need the equivalent of those good properties that housing investment has, for modern digital assets.

The ruling did not answer that question, nor did the outage.

Final Summary

  • A federal judge acquitted Anton and James Peraire-Bueno in a “first of its kind” wire fraud case over a $25M Ethereum exploit, finding that there was no material misrepresentation.
  • The same day, Bitwise CEO Hunter Horsley urged users to hold stablecoins amid major U.S. bank outages, and Vitalik Buterin said digital assets still lack housing’s “safe, non-crazy” default properties.

data.title: Glassnode flags mounting capitulation and realized losses across Bitcoin markets
data.description:
Bitcoin [BTC] traders were down nearly 20% on average. In general, bull market corrections form a bottom at 12% in unrealized losses for the average active trader.

This level of unrealized losses has historically come alongside bottom formations, though it could take at least two months before making a reliable recovery.

Bitcoin holders realized a net loss of 25.8k BTC during the recent sell-off, according to the crypto intelligence platform CryptoQuant. This was the largest 1-day net loss reading since the 13th of July.

The metric uses the price of the coin’s acquisition versus the price at which it was last moved to compute net profit or loss. In early November, the previously positive readings flipped, showing holders were realizing losses.

As Bitcoin prices fell, the net realized losses grew, indicative of investors selling at greater losses. This behavior is commonly seen during bear market phases.

Demand growth contracts at the fastest pace since July

AMBCrypto reported that the leverage flush that led to nearly $3 billion in long liquidations last week might be over, due to the decline in Open Interest.

The importance of sustained demand for a BTC recovery cannot be overstated. However, the market is still in deeply unfavorable conditions for buyers.

The demand growth metric was contracting at a rapid pace, the fastest since early July. The 30-day futures demand growth had been positive in October, but has faded since. The spot demand growth has been negative since the peak in mid-August.

Increased liquidations hastened the perpetuals futures demand contraction, and bearish market sentiment meant the combined total demand growth metric’s 30-day average was -400k BTC.

There were few buyers to absorb the supply being sold.

Capitulation has set in; bulls battle to defend August block

Glassnode presented evidence that spikes in realized losses mirrored past Bitcoin bear markets and represented capitulation episodes. Increased loss-selling has accompanied the sweep of a considerable magnetic zone of liquidations, from $59.5k-$62.2k.

The $62k-$66k block represented a zone where a fifth of the coins in short-term holders’ hands was acquired. The price is already well below the STH cost basis at $74.1k, where recent buyers would be at break-even.

A daily session close below $62k would mean more panic among STH. This could transform a bearish break into a rout, Glassnode warned, making the current block the support bulls must defend.

Final Summary

  • Bitcoin unrealized losses for active traders were at -20%, well below the expected 12% drawdown in a bull market correction.
  • The Bitcoin short-term holder cost basis at $74.1k and the $62k-$66k August block were the two pivotal price regions investors should watch.

data.title: Assessing why Monero crypto’s price slipped below $500 despite major audit news
data.description:
A week ago, MAGIC Grants, the non-profit cryptocurrency research, funding, and blockchain charity, contracted zkSecurity to review the generalized bulletproofs implementation in Monero [XMR] for the Full-Chain Membership Proofs (FCMP++). Monero announced that the audit had been successful, quoting MAGIC Grants’ published findings. It announced that,

“It proves that the Generalized Bulletproofs protocol, in the form Monero implements it, is complete, zero-knowledge, and sound.”

No high or medium severity issues

zkSecurity reviewed the code alongside the cryptography for Generalized Proofs. Commissioned to examine the Generalized Proofs crate within the Monero Oxide project, the audit found no high or medium severity issues.

Four low-severity issues and three informational findings were reported, which the project developers have responded to since.

Generalized Proofs powers the FCMP++ upgrade, a major privacy upgrade for Monero. They are extensions of the standard Bulletproofs zero-knowledge protocol and are modified to support Pedersen vector commitments.

After the code review, zkSecurity wrote a separate proof of the protocol’s security in the Lean theorem prover, which builds machine-checkable mathematical proofs. This independent formalization proved the completeness of the Generalized Proofs protocol in the form Monero currently implements.

Impact on XMR’s price action

The sweep of the late 2025 highs around $600 did not result in a bullish breakout. Instead, the previous week’s sell-off saw XMR close the weekly trading session below $500.

This was only a reset within the broader uptrend the privacy token has enjoyed since 2025. However, the reset could go deeper, below $500. The $390-$440 demand zone was the closest on the weekly chart.

Zooming in, the 4-hour chart showed a short-term selling opportunity. The bearish impulse move to $455 was followed by a bounce to $518, the 78.6% Fibonacci retracement level. XMR slid back towards $500 in the last 24 hours.

This reaction may be a sign that the sellers were back in control, with the DMI’s downtrend highlighting that this could continue.

Final Summary

  • zkSecurity found the Generalized Proofs protocol, in the form Monero implements, “is complete, zero-knowledge, and sound.”
  • XMR has enjoyed a multi-year uptrend, with the recent retracement only part of that uptrend.

data.title: Venice Token reclaims $22 as Arthur Hayes eyes a VVV rally toward $40
data.description:
The utility and access token for the generative platform Venice AI, Venice Token [VVV], has rallied 7.22% in the past 24 hours. It has climbed 17.2% over the past week, putting in a strong performance at a time when most of the rest of crypto was facing selling pressure.

Its daily trading volume has also leapt by 54%, to $54.45 million, according to CoinMarketCap data.

VVV to $40 before the AI bubble bursts

In a post on X, crypto exchange BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes wrote that he expected a Venice Token rally. Three other altcoins, namely Ethereum, NEAR, and ZCash, were also mentioned.

He set a price target of $40 for VVV, as well as $2,800 for ETH, $1,800 for ZEC, and $6 for NEAR.

In May, he had grouped ZEC with Hyperliquid and called for a sizeable rally for both tokens. ZEC nearly reached his $1,000 target shortly thereafter.

On the weekly chart, Venice Token presented an attractive buying opportunity. After the strong rally from $9.81 to $34.61 earlier this year, the altcoin saw a correction, reaching as low as $16.73 a week ago.

However, the weekly trading session did not close below $19.28, the 61.8% Fibonacci retracement level. The bullish reaction after the sweep of this retracement level suggested bulls were beginning to take control of the market.

There was a long way to go, and the wider market sentiment could affect VVV negatively. Based on the evidence at hand, the defense of the $19.8 demand zone indicated bullishness.

The immediate target is the $34 highs, and $40 might be possible, but the route there is unclear.

Short-term VVV outlook flips bullishly

The 4-hour chart displayed a series of lower highs and lower lows in recent weeks, a downtrend. The latest lower high at $19.72 was flipped to support on Monday.

Furthermore, the altcoin has managed to climb past $22.14 and breached the 50% higher timeframe retracement level, too.

Swing traders and long-term investors can look to buy Venice Token. A breakdown below $20.16 will flip the H4 bias bearish, while a drop below $16.74 will signal a deeper correction on the weekly timeframe.

Final Summary

  • Arthur Hayes called for a VVV rally to $40 before the AI boom unwinds.
  • The altcoin’s weekly chart and the sweep of the $19 demand zone were a bullish sign, and the next target is $34.61.

data.title: Top 9 crypto exchanges of November 2026
data.description:
Cryptocurrency exchanges operate by acting as a connecting platform between buyers and sellers. They provide users with a trading platform to create accounts, complete their KYC, deposit and withdraw funds, and start trading in the supported cryptocurrencies.

Users can access features like spot, futures, and derivatives trading. There are wallets available that allow them to store, deposit, and withdraw digital assets. Crypto exchanges make markets accessible to individuals and institutions around the world and provide liquidity. Here is our list of the top 9 crypto exchanges of November 2026:

1. Binance

Binance was established in 2017 and is one of the biggest crypto exchanges in the world. It has evolved into one of the most comprehensive ecosystems that caters to retail investors, developers, and institutional customers.

It has a lot of trading services, including spot, margin, futures, and peer-to-peer trading in supported markets. There are also advanced charting tools, trading indicators, various order types, and market analysis that support different types of trading.

2. OKX

Founded in 2017, OKX has developed a broader ecosystem over time that includes Web3 services, derivatives, cryptocurrency trading, and blockchain-related products. The platform is a great pick for retail users, and professional traders alike.

It has the options of spot trading, margin trading, futures, and perpetual swaps. There are market charts, technical indicators, order management features and tools that are designed for amateur and experienced traders.

3. Kraken

Kraken was founded in 2011 and is one of the oldest exchanges in the space. It supports cryptocurrency buying, selling, and spot trading while the Kraken Pro platform has advanced trading options that include market charts, order books, technical analysis and different order execution options.

There are margin trading, futures, staking options also available on the platform. They have a strong focus on security which includes measures like encryption, account protection features, two-factor authentication, and secure digital asset custody arrangements.

4. Bitget

Bitget has spot and futures trading along with other digital asset trading options. It has real-time market information, technical charts, trading indicators, and order management features. Copy trading is one of its major distinctive products that lets users replicate trading strategies from other traders on the platform.

There are security measures like withdrawal controls, risk monitoring and asset protection mechanisms in place to ensure user safety. They also support a lot of crypto and trading pairs letting users access to different digital asset markets.

5. KuCoin

KuCoin has a wide range of cryptocurrencies and trading services and provides traders access to digital assets, spot trading, margin trading, and futures. There are trading charts, technical indicators, multiple order types, trading charts and market information.

There are also trading bots available that allow users to automate selected trading strategies. Lending-related products, and wallet integrations are also part of the KuCoin platform.

6. Crypto.com

Crypto.com was established in 2016 and created a broad ecosystem over the years that includes cryptocurrency trading, payments, digital wallets, and other blockchain-related products. It also has a crypto wallet, payment-related products and eligible digital asset earning programmes.

The security measures on Crypto.com include multi-factor authentication, withdrawal protection, digital asset custody controls and account monitoring. The exchange is also known for its customer-oriented approach and efforts to connect crypto services with everyday financial activities.

7. Bitfinex

Bitfinex offers margin trading, spot trading and derivatives products along with lending and funding related services in supported markets. There are detailed order books, customizable trading layouts, advanced charts and multiple order charts.

The advanced trading interface and liquidity infrastructure distinguish it from platforms designed primarily for beginners. In terms of security measures as well, Bitfinex has monitoring mechanisms in place and multi-factor authentication as well.

8. Coinbase

Coinbase started out in 2012 and has developed its services beyond cryptocurrency buying and selling to include institutional custody, and many blockchain-related products that are useful for advanced and beginner users. It was created with the vision of making crypto accessible through a secure and user-friendly digital platform.

The platform has an Advanced trading experience that lets traders use features such as real-time market charts, order books, price indicators, and advanced order execution options. Coinbase Prime gives eligible institutions access to trading, custody, and other digital asset infrastructure.

9. Gate

Gate supports a wide range of digital assets and crypto trading pairs. Its ecosystem has options like spot trading, margin trading, futures trading, digital asset management, Web3 services, and derivatives.

Gate supports 5,400 digital assets and has over 63 million users around the world with lightning-fast listings for new and trending tokens.

Conclusion

Crypto exchanges are an essential part of the global financial system and important towards driving mainstream crypto adoption. Exchanges connect individuals, businesses, institutional investors and financial markets and aren’t just trading platforms but also enablers of digital adoption.

As with any financial decision, users should conduct their own research, review an exchange’s security measures and fee structure, and fully understand the risks involved before committing significant funds.

data.title: Bitcoin miner fees hit a 15-year low – Why profit margins are shrinking
data.description:
As 2026 is nearing its end, Bitcoin [BTC] miners are facing growing financial pressure. This, in turn has resulted in miners increasingly selling their Bitcoin reserves instead of holding them for long-term appreciation.

According to Glassnode’s recent update, publicly listed Bitcoin miners have sold nearly half of their Bitcoin holdings since January 2026.

This means that miners are increasingly treating their Bitcoin reserves as a source of liquidity to fund business operations and maybe for expansion into AI data centers.

Double trouble for Bitcoin miners

At the same time, there is also a decline in transaction fee revenue. With 11 months into 2026, Bitcoin miners earned just 912 BTC in transaction fees, the lowest annual total since at least 2011. This is a huge drop compared to 1,720 BTC in 2025 and 15,178 BTC in 2024.

In other words, transaction fees accounted for only 0.63% of total miner revenue in 2026, down from 1% in 2025 and 6.5% in 2023. This is enough proof that demand for Bitcoin block space has weakened, reducing the contribution of this revenue source.

Execs join the fray

Remarking on the same, CleanSpark CBO Harry Sudock said,

Like with any commodity production business, it should get harder and thinner margin over time because the lowest cost operators should be the most successful and durable.

In other words, Sudock believes Bitcoin mining will become increasingly competitive over the next decade, with shrinking profit margins favoring operators with the lowest production and electricity costs.

He expects the global hashrate to continue growing, but at a slower pace than in the previous ten years, as mining hardware becomes more efficient and large publicly listed miners explore AI data centers.

He also argued that Bitcoin mining will not depend solely on large public companies, as smaller businesses and privately held miners can operate profitably.

At the same time, CryptoQuant CEO Ki Young Ju noted that Bitcoin’s average mining cost reached approximately $62,862 in Q3 2026, based on Marathon Digital’s filings. With BTC trading near this level, miners are facing shrinking profit margins and could face potential losses if prices fall further.

However, the relatively high hashrate suggests miners remain committed to the network despite growing profitability concerns.

Bitcoin miners face a tough time, but…

This comes as Bitcoin miners are shifting their focus towards AI and high-performance computing (HPC), as investors increasingly value their power infrastructure and data centers.

Companies such as Core Scientific, IREN, and TeraWulf are generating significant revenue from AI infrastructure and HPC services, in some cases surpassing their Bitcoin mining income.

However, the Miner Outflow chart suggests that compared with the rest of the year, November outflows are calm.

At the same time, the Miner Reserve chart was at about 1.1925 million BTC at press time. In fact, through October and into November, it moved in a narrow band, roughly between 1.192 million and 1.1926 million.

All in all, miners are roughly holding steady, with small accumulation or lower net selling.

Final Summary

  • Bitcoin miners earned just 912 BTC in transaction fees, the lowest annual total since at least 2011.
  • Execs believe Bitcoin mining will become increasingly competitive over the next decade, with shrinking profit margins.

data.title: How did Coinbase stop deepfake Elon Musk’s promise to double your crypto?
data.description:
Scammers recently used a fake video of Elon Musk to get people to send them crypto. It didn’t go to plan.

Especially since according to Coinbase, it blocked a big chunk of those transfers before the money could disappear.

A fake Musk livestream drew 500K viewers…

… and Coinbase stopped $4.7 million from reaching scammers.

Someone put out a YouTube livestream made to look like a Tesla flying car demo. On screen was an AI-made Elon Musk, and the pitch was to send crypto and get 2x back.

More than half a million people tuned in. The stream flashed wallet addresses and QR codes. So, sending money took just a scan.

In a blog post, Coinbase laid out what happened. In about two hours, hundreds of its users tried to send funds to the scammers. Its automated fraud system caught about 91% of that.

The real Musk had nothing to do with any of it.

Here, it’s worth pointing out that Coinbase hasn’t said how much of the remaining 9% actually got through.

Coinbase fought AI with AI

data.title: XRP price’s plan to break past $1 depends on ETF flows, sentiment, and…
data.description:
At press time, XRP seemed to be attempting to stage a short-term recovery on the 4-hour chart. Unfortunately, persistent institutional outflows and a critical technical hurdle at the $1.00-level have been keeping the altcoin’s bullish hopes in check.

ETF flows show sustained bleeding

As per data for 17th November, U.S Spot XRP ETFs saw net outflows of $6.14 million. This bleeding was mainly concentrated in two products — The Canary XRP ETF (XRPC) saw $5.01 million leave the fund, while the Grayscale XRP Trust ETF (GXRP) recorded outflows of $1.12 million.

These outflows were in line with XRP Spot ETFs’ broader trend. For the uninitiated, the week ending 13th November saw outflows of $19.1 million — the largest single-week withdrawal in nearly eight months.

That’s not all either as the recent exodus also hinted at a lack of institutional conviction around XRP’s press time price levels.

A visible short-term bounce?

AMBCrypto’s look at XRP’s 4-hour chart hinted at the altcoin showing signs of life following a steep downtrend that bottomed out near $0.89 on 15th November.

At the time of writing, the price was hovering at $0.9979 after having been rejected from its 24-hour high of $1.0078.

However, momentum indicators appeared to be turning positive. The Relative Strength Index (RSI) had crossed above the neutral line, sitting at 55.19 at press time. This implied that buyers were regaining control.

Furthermore, the MACD registered a bullish crossover, with the histogram flashing green bars — a signal that short-term momentum may be shifting to the upside.

XRP price prediction: A make-or-break moment?

The 4-hour chart recorded XRP struggling to break the $1.00-$1.01 psychological barrier, in line with the top of its recent consolidation.

If XRP can secure a 4-hour close above $1.0078, it would confirm a short-term breakout. Its next target will then be $1.05, followed by $1.09.

And yet, it is likely that XRP can face a rejection at $1.00. This will then cause a retest of the $0.95 support zone. Conversely, a break below $0.94 would expose $0.89 to further falls.

Conclusion

XRP’s 4-hour MACD and RSI hinted at a relief rally. On the contrary, XRP’s $6.1 million ETF outflows and its hard resistance at $1.00 suggested that traders should still remain cautious.

In the short term, unless XRP can close above $1.01, it will remain vulnerable to a pullback.

Final Summary

  • U.S Spot XRP ETFs recorded 6.14 million in outflows on 17th November as institutional sell-offs continued.
  • XRP must close above the $1.01 resistance to break out towards $1.05.
